findings.title: Java MessageFormat syntax breaks Account UI interpolation
findings.body: This file is consumed by the JavaScript Account UI, whose translations use i18next-style {{0}} placeholders, as shown by the surrounding entries. Changing error-invalid-multivalued-size to Java MessageFormat syntax '{0} ... {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' means the UI will not interpolate the values and will render the literal placeholders/choice syntax to users. The same change in js/apps/admin-ui messages_en.properties has the same problem; the MessageFormat form is only appropriate for the Java theme properties.

findings.title: Java MessageFormat syntax breaks Admin UI interpolation
findings.body: This Admin UI resource uses i18next-style {{0}} placeholders, but error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed to '{0} ... {2,choice,...}'. The Admin UI does not evaluate Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat, so users will see literal {0}/{1} and choice syntax instead of the attribute size limits. The Java-style text should be confined to themes/src/main/resources Java message bundles.

findings.title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian (lt) value for totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' when removing the disallowed anchor tags. Lithuanian users will now see an Italian instruction on the TOTP setup page. The same wrong Italian string was also inserted into themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties loginTotpStep1.

findings.title: Diff-trimming can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of reporting illegal HTML
findings.body: The start/end trimming loops are computed independently and can overlap when the value and sanitized strings share repeated prefix/suffix characters (for example value 'aaa' vs sanitized 'aa': start advances to 2 and end advances to 2). Then value.substring(start, value.length()-end) is called with start greater than the end index, throwing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. A malformed translation therefore crashes the verifier instead of producing the intended 'Illegal HTML' message.

findings.title: Missing English bundle aborts verification with an unchecked exception
findings.body: verifySafeHtml derives the English file by regex-replacing the locale suffix and path segment, and throws RuntimeException if that file cannot be opened. verify() only documents/handles MojoExecutionException and only catches IOException around the call, so a properties file without a matching _en.properties at the derived location (new locale directory, non-standard layout, or a base messages.properties) aborts the whole verification run instead of reporting a per-file problem or skipping/comparing sensibly.

findings.title: Any English HTML unlocks all allowed HTML tags in translations
findings.body:
containsHtml only tests whether the English value contains any ''; if true, the translation is checked with POLICY_SOME_HTML allowing br, p, strong and b regardless of which tags the English source actually uses. A translator can therefore add

/
// markup to a message whose English source only contains, for example, a or an anchor, contrary to the stated intent of allowing HTML in translations only mirroring the source. The policy should be derived from the tags present in the English value, as is done for anchors.
